ex-E101-1.title: Distances of different planets from the Sun
ex-E101-1.question:
Jupiter and Saturn are two large planets composed mostly of gases.

(a) Light minute is another unit of length. A light minute is the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in one minute. Jupiter is about 43.2 light minutes from the Sun.

(i) How long does it take for light to travel from the Sun to Jupiter?

(ii) Express the distance between the Sun and Jupiter in metres.

(b) The distance between the Sun and Saturn is about 9.5 AU.

(i) Express the distance in metres.

(ii) Estimate the time needed for the light from the Sun to reach Saturn. Give your answer in seconds.

Take the speed of light c = 3.00 × 108 m s–1.
ex-E101-1.answer:
(a) (i) 43.2 minutes

(ii) 43.2 light minutes = 43.2 × (3.00 × 108) × 60

= 7.78 × 1011 m

(b) (i) 9.5 AU = 9.5 × 1.50 × 1011 m

= 1.425 × 1012 m

≈ 1.43 × 1012 m

(ii) Time needed = 1.425 × 10123.00 × 108 = 4750 s

ex-E101-2.title: Position of Venus in its orbit
ex-E101-2.question:
Several photographs of Venus were taken on different days over a period of time (Fig a).

(a) Refer to Figure b. X, Y and Z are three positions in Venus’ orbit. Determine the direction of movement of Venus around the Sun.

(b) What is the position of Venus, X, Y or Z, when its new phase is observed? Explain.
ex-E101-2.answer:
(a) X → Y → Z

(b) Z.

The observer is on the opposite side of Venus as the Sun is.
